news.title: Putin wants peace more than Zelensky: Trump
news.text: US President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin appeared more willing than Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to reach a peace agreement, even as questions mounted over alleged Russian violations of a proposed energy ceasefire. "I think, actually, Putin wants to make a deal more than Zelensky," Trump told reporters at the White House before departing for a political rally in Ohio. His remarks came as reporters pressed him on Russia's continued strikes against Ukraine and whether Moscow had agreed to his proposal for halting attacks on energy infrastructure. Trump insisted that both countries supported the ceasefire initiative, although a reporter pointed out that Putin had not publicly committed to it. "I think they both support it. I think they want to make a deal, but they don't know how. But we're going to get them to make a deal," he said. Asked specifically how he intended to persuade Putin to abide by the proposed ceasefire, Trump again placed emphasis on securing Zelensky's agreement. "Well, I think what's happening is he wants to make a deal, and we have to get Zelensky to want to make a deal," the President said. The exchange underscored Trump's continued confidence that he could broker an agreement between Moscow and Kyiv, despite the absence of a publicly confirmed ceasefire accepted by both governments. When a reporter challenged his earlier assertion that Russia and Ukraine had already agreed to a ceasefire, Trump stood by his account. "Well, they agreed, you know why? Because I said you agree, that's why. They agreed because I said they agreed and that thing has to get settled," he said. The President did not provide details of any formal understanding between the two countries or explain how the proposed arrangement would be monitored and enforced. Asked about reports that Russia had violated the ceasefire by attacking Ukraine overnight, Trump said he needed to examine the circumstances. "I'm not sure about that and we'll take a look," he said. He subsequently suggested that responsibility for violations was not confined to Moscow. "Well, I'd have to look at it and see because there's been violations on both sides," Trump said. The President also cited what he described as mounting casualties in the conflict, arguing that the continued loss of life made a negotiated settlement urgent. "This month, they lost 32,000 people in that war, and it's ridiculous. So, they have to get together and get it done," he said. Trump later repeated the figure, describing those killed as predominantly young soldiers. He did not identify the source of the estimate, which could not be independently verified from his remarks. Asked what message he had for Putin after Zelensky reportedly expressed support for an energy ceasefire, Trump maintained that an agreement remained possible. "Well, we're going to see what happens. We'll get it done," he said. Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022 and has produced years of fighting, extensive destruction of civilian infrastructure and heavy military and civilian casualties. Both governments have repeatedly accused the other of attacking energy facilities and other targets.
news.summary: Trump claimed both sides supported his proposed energy ceasefire initiative but acknowledged uncertainty over reported violations by Russia and Ukraine. He said he would examine the allegations and stressed the urgent need for negotiations, citing heavy casualties in the ongoing war
news.author: Abhishek Trivedi

news.title: Vivek Ramaswamy and Ohio Governor’s race: The polls are missing the bigger picture
news.text:
The polls in Ohio’s gubernatorial race are all over the place right now, and in my view, not particularly reliable. Recent surveys have produced dramatically different results, ranging from a narrow lead for Republican Vivek Ramaswamy to a sizable advantage for Democrat Amy Acton.
My assessment of the race rests on several political, cultural and economic factors that I believe deserve greater attention than any single poll.
Ohio was once one of America’s most important presidential battleground states. That political identity has changed considerably. Donald Trump carried Ohio in 2016, 2020 and 2024, winning the most recent election by approximately 11 percentage points.
Although presidential voting patterns do not automatically translate into gubernatorial results, particularly during midterm elections, such clear and consistent recent voter preferences for Conservatives, Republicans and President Trump cannot be easily ignored or dismissed.
I also believe ideological developments within the Democratic Party could influence conservative turnout. The growing influence of DSA (Democratic Socialists Party of America) aligned democratic socialists, Marxist political ideas and Islamists among Democrats' concerns and many conservatives, including me. I expect these concerns to be part of the political conversation leading up to November.
The Trump and Vance factor
Trump's endorsement is a major feature of Vivek’s campaign, particularly in a state where Trump won decisively in 2024. Trump’s October 3 rally in Vandalia brought national attention to Ohio's Republican candidates and demonstrated his continued involvement in the state's political contests.
The question now is how strongly Trump's Maga base will participate in the midterm election. The enthusiasm of these voters, their response to Trump's endorsement, and their eventual turnout could significantly influence the gubernatorial race.
Vice President JD Vance adds another dimension. Vance has endorsed Vivek and publicly described him as a dear friend. Their close relationship brings together two nationally prominent Republicans with strong Ohio connections.
Vance's October 9 appearance in Lima further highlighted that relationship and his public support for Vivek's candidacy.
Acton debate controversy
Amy Acton's refusal to participate in proposed debates with Vivek has become another issue in the campaign.
Vivek has expressed his willingness to debate, while Acton's campaign has defended its decision by citing concerns about political attacks.
I regard public debates as an important opportunity for candidates to demonstrate leadership, defend their records and respond directly to criticism.
In my view, Acton's refusal risks creating an impression of weakness, particularly when her opponent has publicly welcomed the opportunity for direct exchanges.
Her supporters may interpret the decision differently, but I believe voters are entitled to expect candidates for governor to answer difficult questions in an open forum.
Vivek’s Hindu faith
Vivek has been completely upfront from the beginning about his Indian heritage and Hindu faith. He has never attempted to conceal or downplay either, even while campaigning in a country where evangelical Christians form an important part of the conservative electorate.
I consider that openness significant. It gives evangelical Christian voters ample time to become familiar with Vivek, understand his religious and cultural background, and evaluate his political positions and personal character well before Election Day.
By November, neither his Hindu faith nor his Indian roots will come as a surprise. In my view, this extended period of familiarity is an important factor that deserves more attention in assessments of the Ohio race. It allows voters to form their judgments with a fuller understanding of the candidate rather than reacting to something they have only recently discovered.
Ohio is largely a working-class state, shaped by generations of manufacturing, industry, and hard work. Yet there is also something deeply American about respecting grit, entrepreneurship, ambition, and individual success.
Vivek represents an American success story: the son of Indian immigrants who built successful businesses and became enormously wealthy before entering politics.
I have always regarded America's admiration for achievement as one of its defining cultural strengths. The country has a long tradition of celebrating entrepreneurs and individuals who build successful enterprises through ambition, ingenuity, and determination.
I believe that basic American respect for achievement is more important to understanding the country's character than resentment or jealousy of another person's success. Vivek's personal story brings that cultural question directly into the Ohio election.
The economy could change the political environment
Finally, conditions between now and Election Day could substantially change the political environment.
If the war situation moves more in America's favour, oil prices decline, inflation continues to improve, everyday prices begin moving in the right direction and the Trump administration's infrastructure and investment initiatives start producing visible economic results, the political atmosphere could change considerably.
These developments would be particularly relevant in a Rust Belt state such as Ohio, where manufacturing, industrial investment, employment, and household purchasing power remain central economic concerns.
The timing of economic changes matters. Even modest improvements in household finances or business confidence could influence how voters assess the country's direction before November.
Taking these factors together, my view of the Ohio race differs from the picture presented by some recent polls.
Ohio's increasingly conservative electoral history, Trump's decisive 2024 victory, his endorsement of Vivek, JD Vance's friendship and support, the debate controversy, Vivek's openness about his heritage and faith, America's respect for entrepreneurial success and the possibility of improving economic conditions all form part of my assessment.
I believe these considerations deserve to be examined together rather than treating individual polling results as definitive.
My personal forecast is a Vivek Ramaswamy victory by approximately 3 to 4 percentage points over Amy Acton. That is my own political judgement, based on how I interpret the factors shaping the race, rather than a statistical projection.
(Vinson Xavier Palathingal is an Indian American conservative activist, based in Fort Myers, FL He campaigned for Vivek Ramaswamy during his presidential run in 2024. Views expressed in the above piece are personal and solely those of the author. They do not necessarily reflect Firstpost’s views.)

news.title: US Places Nigeria on Blacklist, Threatens to Cut Military Aid
news.text:
The United States has placed Nigeria on its Child Soldiers Prevention Act (CSPA) blacklist, a decision that could restrict military assistance, weapons sales and defence cooperation from October 1, 2026, unless President Donald Trump grants a waiver.

The designation was contained in the US Department of State’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, which identified Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) as armed groups that continue to recruit, abduct and use children in Nigeria.

The report, published on October 11, assessed Nigeria’s efforts to combat human trafficking between April 1, 2025, and March 31, 2026.

It also raised concerns about official corruption, the prosecution of trafficking-related crimes and the protection provided to victims.

Nigeria was listed among 14 countries facing scrutiny under the Child Soldiers Prevention Act.

Other countries named include Russia, Iran, Somalia, South Sudan and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Under the American law, countries on the list may face restrictions on specific forms of security assistance and the commercial licensing of military equipment.

The measures cover International Military Education and Training, Foreign Military Financing, Excess Defence Articles and certain peacekeeping assistance.

The report explained that the restrictions would take effect from October 1, 2026, subject to a presidential waiver, an applicable exception or the reinstatement of assistance under the law.

It stated, “Governments identified on the list are subject to restrictions, in the following fiscal year, on certain security assistance and commercial licensing of military equipment.”

The report added that the law also prohibits licences for direct commercial sales of military equipment to listed governments, although exceptions may apply under specified circumstances.

The development comes amid security cooperation between Washington and Abuja, as both countries continue efforts to combat terrorism and other security threats.

Any restrictions on military assistance could therefore create additional complications for their defence relationship, depending on the programmes affected and whether the US president grants an exemption.

The report identified Boko Haram and ISWAP as the groups responsible for recruiting and using children in armed activities.

It said children as young as 12 were forced into various roles, including cooking, domestic work, spying, carrying messages, guarding checkpoints and participating in combat operations.

It stated, “Boko Haram and ISIS-West Africa continue recruiting, abducting, and using—including through force, fraud, and coercion—child soldiers as young as 12 years old as cooks, domestic workers, spies, porters, messengers, bodyguards or guards at checkpoints, ‘morality police,’ armed combatants, and suicide bombers in attacks in Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad, and Niger; these children are subjected to physical and sexual abuse and forced drug use.”

According to the report, the armed groups also continue to abduct women and girls, subjecting many to forced labour, forced marriage and sexual slavery.

It further alleged that some girls were punished for refusing marriage by being forced to carry out suicide attacks.

The document raised additional concerns about the treatment of victims after their release from captivity.

It alleged that, in some cases, government authorities compelled victims of forced marriage to return to their Boko Haram husbands through demobilisation centres in Borno State.

Beyond the activities of insurgent groups, the report highlighted the involvement of criminal gangs in trafficking and the exploitation of children.

It said some gangs in southern Nigeria recruit children for forced criminal activities, including kidnapping and robbery, while also exploiting them in sex trafficking.

In the northwest, criminal networks were reported to exploit victims in forced labour in agriculture and mining.

The report also examined Nigeria’s wider record in combating human trafficking, stating that the country had failed to meet the US government’s minimum standards for eliminating trafficking for the 15th consecutive year, although it acknowledged some efforts by the Nigerian authorities.

One of the major concerns was the absence of reported investigations, prosecutions or convictions involving government officials allegedly complicit in trafficking crimes.

“The government did not report any investigations, prosecutions, or convictions of government employees allegedly complicit in trafficking crimes or provide details or other actions taken against complicit officials from previous years,” the report stated.

It added that “corruption and official complicity in trafficking crimes remained significant concerns.”

The US report further noted that “observers reported some law enforcement, military, and other government officials reportedly committed trafficking crimes, accepted bribes to facilitate trafficking, or obstructed justice by interfering with investigations.”

These findings raised questions about accountability within public institutions and the enforcement of existing anti-trafficking laws.

On law enforcement, Nigerian authorities investigated 1,341 trafficking cases during the reporting period.

The cases included 589 involving sex trafficking, 301 related to forced labour and 451 that were not classified by specific category. The investigations involved 1,367 suspects.

However, the report recorded 94 prosecutions and 97 convictions during the period.

It acknowledged that most convicted traffickers received prison sentences of at least one year and noted increased cooperation between Nigerian authorities and foreign governments on international trafficking investigations.

Such cooperation reportedly supported operations across West Africa and Southeast Asia, including activities conducted in partnership with INTERPOL.

The number of identified trafficking victims also remained a concern.

Authorities identified 2,004 victims, comprising 893 victims of sex trafficking and 1,111 victims of forced labour.

However, only 675 received government-supported assistance during the reporting period, compared with 2,058 in the previous year.

The report criticised conditions in shelters operated by the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP).

It said the agency’s closed-shelter policy restricted residents’ freedom of movement and affected children’s access to education.

According to the document, “residents were not allowed freedom of movement, including children’s access to school.”

It also noted that “access to some protection services was tied to victims’ willingness to cooperate with law enforcement proceedings.”

The report said adult victims who declined shelter accommodation were not offered alternative services.

It further observed that only one dedicated non-governmental organisation shelter was available for adult male trafficking survivors.

These concerns suggested that access to protection remained a challenge for some victims, particularly those unwilling or unable to participate in criminal proceedings against their traffickers.

Despite the criticisms, the US acknowledged increased Nigerian government spending on anti-trafficking activities. Funding for victim services rose from N128 million to N233 million, while spending on prevention increased from N58.8 million to N245 million.

The government also coordinated the repatriation of 428 Nigerians who had been exploited abroad, obtained restitution for 14 victims as part of criminal sentences and maintained anti-trafficking task forces in 23 states.

However, the report identified gaps in labour protection and the regulation of recruitment practices.

It said the government had not prohibited worker-paid recruitment fees, reported holding labour recruiters liable for fraudulent recruitment through civil and criminal proceedings, or provided specialised training on child labour and human trafficking to labour inspectors.

It also stated that the government had not provided anti-trafficking training to its diplomatic personnel.

The report raised concerns about international criminal networks allegedly using Nigeria as a base for organised online fraud.

It stated that “highly organised foreign criminal syndicates fraudulently recruit foreigners to Nigeria with promises of employment, confine them in leased properties and compel them to participate in organised online scams.”

It also alleged that Russian authorities fraudulently recruited Nigerians to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war.

The report further claimed that Nigeria’s Ministry of Education helped promote Russia’s Alabuga Start programme despite warning signs.

The document additionally raised concerns about possible forced labour involving North Korean nationals working in Nigeria.

Another issue highlighted was the continued operation of so-called baby factories, which are criminal enterprises disguised as orphanages, maternity homes or religious centres.

According to the report, women held in these facilities are sometimes sexually abused and forced to give birth to children who are subsequently sold.

The operations were described as a documented feature of Nigeria’s trafficking problem, particularly in the southern part of the country.

The US government said Nigeria serves as a source, transit and destination country for human trafficking.

The country’s ranking in the annual TIP Report has fluctuated between Tier 1, Tier 2 and the Tier 2 Watch List. Nigeria last attained Tier 1 status in 2011.

The CSPA designation is separate from Nigeria’s broader trafficking ranking, although both assessments reflect concerns about the country’s efforts to prevent exploitation and protect vulnerable people.

When contacted for comments, NAPTIP’s Head of Press and Public Relations, Vincent Adekoye, said the agency would make its response to the report public.

The Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, did not respond to calls to his mobile telephone or a text message seeking the Presidency’s reaction.

The implications of the blacklist will depend partly on the scope of any restrictions imposed and whether the US administration grants Nigeria a waiver.

Without an applicable exemption, the country could face limitations on certain military training programmes, financing arrangements, equipment transfers and commercial defence sales.

news.title: Protester punched in face by Trump supporter, mocked by president at Ohio rally: ‘Gotta go on a diet’
news.text:
A heckler wearing a “Release the Epstein Files” shirt was punched in the face by an apparent supporter of President Donald Trump during a rally Monday in Youngstown, Ohio, before the president mocked the protester’s weight.

Trump was criticizing Ohio Democratic Senate candidate Sherrod Brown, who is challenging Republican Sen. Jon Husted after losing his Senate seat in 2024, when rally attendees shifted their attention toward a confrontation in the crowd.

Video of the confrontation showed a rallygoer who appeared to support Trump shoving the heckler and striking her in the face as the crowd chanted “USA!”

TRUMP TOUTS ‘GOLDEN AGE’ AT OHIO RALLY, URGES VOTERS TO DELIVER GOP MIDTERM WINS

A heckler wearing a “Release the Epstein Files” shirt was punched in the face by a supporter of President Donald Trump during a rally. (Kent NISHIMURA / AFP via Getty Images)

The man also grabbed the woman by the hair and attempted to slam her face toward the ground.

Police eventually intervened and broke up the fight before escorting the woman out of the venue. Video showed the man who struck her remaining in the arena and exchanging high-fives with other attendees.

Trump appeared to notice the disruption and accused the protester of being paid to interrupt the rally, although he offered no evidence to support the allegation. He also mocked the protester’s weight.

ANTI-TRUMP PROTESTER CHARGED AFTER VIRAL VIDEO APPEARS TO SHOW JOURNALIST SHOVED AT MAINE PROTEST

Police intervened and broke up the fight before escorting the woman out of the venue. (Kent NISHIMURA / AFP via Getty Images)

“He’s a paid protester,” Trump said, appearing to be unaware that the heckler was a woman. “They’re all paid. They get paid by the lefties in order to destroy our country. They’re scum. But he’s going back home to Mom. He’s going back home to Mom. Look at him. Look at him. Terrible. Don’t we love law enforcement? Oh, he’s gotta go on a diet! He’s a fat guy. Wow. Wow. Gotta go on a diet fast. We all do.”

“No, they’re paid protesters. That’s a very low-class protester,” the president added.

The woman’s “Release the Epstein Files” shirt comes as Trump and his Justice Department face bipartisan scrutiny over the delay in the release of additional documents related to the investigations into deceased sex predator Jeffrey Epstein.

President Donald Trump claimed the woman was a paid protester who was fat and should go on a diet. (Kent NISHIMURA / AFP via Getty Images)

Just days before the fight on Monday, there was a fight at another Trump rally in San Antonio, Texas, where a man wearing a MAGA hat grabbed a heckler by the hair and pulled him to the ground.

news.title: I heard the full 6-minute recording behind the James Talarico hoax. Here's what's actually in it
news.text:
Around 9am on Sunday, I received several frantic calls and texts from a Republican operative who claimed to have proof that James Talarico, the Democratic Senate candidate on the verge of turning Texas blue for the first time in decades, had checked into a mental health facility for psychiatric care.

The so-called proof was a six-minute recording of a phone call to the Lindner Center of Hope, a hospital in Mason, Ohio more than 1,000 miles from Talarico's hometown of Austin.

An edited version of the recording was later made public on social media and spread like wildfire before it was debunked.

In the audio, a staff member repeatedly says she cannot find a patient by Talarico's name. First she says there is no record of him being there in the past four days and later, she contradicts herself and says he had been 'discharged this evening… that's why I don't have it.'

The health facility has since stated that Talarico 'never received treatment' there and Talarico responded to the audio by saying he has never even been to Ohio.

Like many other reporters in Texas and across the country, I had been looking into why Talarico mysteriously took 10 days off in the middle of a historic election and one of the most watched campaigns in the country.

His absence included canceling public events, as well as private fundraisers, something rarely done in such a high-stakes race.

Talarico, 37, reappeared at an Austin music festival on Friday and his campaign team had maintained since September 30 that the diabetic candidate was suffering from a bad bout of flu. But false rumors had been circulating in Republican circles that he had been struggling with his mental health under the pressure of campaigning and that he may have sought treatment in Ohio.

When I was approached with the recording on Sunday, I was told the Daily Mail had to publish the recording 'immediately'.

We declined.

There were serious questions about the recording's authenticity and about how the information had been obtained, and whether Talarico's privacy had been violated in the process.

Unhappy with that answer, the caller, Rhein Amacher- whose real name is Ryan- who claims to be a former Trump staffer, gave the recording to paid GOP influencer Nick Sortor.

Sortor published an edited version of the call on X on Sunday afternoon, where it racked up millions of views in a matter of hours and caught the attention of Elon Musk, who boosted it by commenting: '!!'

Within hours, the Ohio health center shut down the rumors, stating that the young politician has 'never received treatment from Lindner Center of Hope.'

In the unedited recording given to the Daily Mail, Amacher poses as a man named 'Tim' who is trying to send a care package to his cousin, Talarico.

It was his second call to the center. On the first, he had been told he could not get any information without a code from the patient.

In his second attempt, Amacher gives a fake code, which the staff member struggles to match to any patient.

'He must have checked out then,' Amacher suggests.

'I do not see that name here, so maybe he's been discharged,' says the staff member, who appears to be an elderly woman.

Amacher presses her on when he left. After a long pause, she comes back on the line: 'I do not find anyone by that name for the last four days, that's been discharged, and they're not here in the building.'

Only when Amacher keeps pushing does she contradict herself: 'What is today… looks like he was just discharged this evening. That's why I don't have it.'

That line was the one featured in the shortened clip that went viral. But the timeline does not add up.

Amacher admits he made the call on Saturday night, when Talarico and his girlfriend were in the front row at a Kacey Musgraves concert in Austin.

When I asked Amacher to explain the discrepancy on Monday morning, he said: 'You can basically discharge without paperwork, and you know, the paperwork usually follows.

'It's not all at once, but she confirmed that he was there. The dates might not line up perfectly.'

Amacher, a Republican who wants Ken Paxton to win the election, says he came up with the idea of calling the Ohio facility after it was circulated online as the place Talarico had spent his time off.

'[Talarico] … doesn't get called out enough,' he told the Daily Mail.

'I'm not afraid to get my hands dirty. I want the public to know what he's been doing.'

He denies being paid by Paxton, Talarico's opponent in the Senate race.

Paxton's team helped fuel the speculation last week by tipping off reporters about potential mental health issues. His campaign alleged, without proof, that Talarico, was not recovering from flu but had suffered a mental breakdown and checked into a mental health facility.

Legal experts said Talarico likely has grounds to sue Amacher for trying to obtain his private health information, which is protected under federal law.

Asked whether he was afraid of being sued, Amacher said he had yet to hear anything directly from Talarico or his campaign.

'I didn't do anything wrong. All I said was I want to send him a care package. They can confirm or deny that was a patient there. I just asked to send a care package. I could say I was Santa Claus for all I care.'

Friends have advised him to keep a low profile, he said, but he will appear on a cable TV network tonight to defend his work.

It comes as polls suggest Talarico, a former schoolteacher, could pull off a stunning Midterms upset in a state Donald Trump won by nearly 14 points in 2024.

A victory for Talarico on November 3 would make him the first Democrat elected to the US Senate from Texas since 1988.
news.summary: I had been looking into why Talarico mysteriously took 10 days off in the middle of a historic election and one of the most watched campaigns in the country.
news.author: Editor,Maryann Martinez

news.title: Donald Trump appears in new Mike Tyson documentary to discuss rape case
news.text: Mike Tyson may have weakened his own case by testifying in the 1992 trial over his rape of Desiree Washington. That's according to the president of the United States, Donald Trump , who gives his account in a new Netflix documentary. Tyson, 60, was convicted of raping then-18-year-old beauty pageant contestant Washington at the Canterbury Hotel in July 1991. The boxing icon was sentenced to six years in prison , though he ultimately served only three before his release in March 1995. President Trump was involved in Tyson's career at the time and helped promote several of his fights in the late 1980s and early '90s. The Convention Hall in Atlantic City, New Jersey, which was connected to Trump Plaza, hosted bouts against the likes of Michael Spinks, Carl Williams and Alex Stewart. Specifically, Trump has suggested Tyson may have harmed his own defence by giving testimony. 'The Baddest Man on the Planet' testified in an Indianapolis court for 78 minutes, insisting his encounter with Washington was consensual, which led to accusations of inconsistencies in his account from the prosecution. JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page "I think Mike shouldn't have testified," said the sitting president during his cameo on the docuseries, TYSON, which premieres on Tuesday. Trump was himself found liable for the sexual abuse and defamation of writer E Jean Carroll in a federal civil jury in 2023. "I'm not sure that he did a bad job in testifying. But one thing with Mike, he's very truthful. And I think the truth hurt him...in this case." TYSON features accounts from those close to the famed boxer, as well as his personal bodyguard and others. One friend, Dawn Milhouse, suggests he "never stood a chance" of winning the trial in Indianapolis due to alleged racist roots in the state. However, the third episode of the series also features an account from Dr. Thomas Richardson, an emergency room physician at Methodist Hospital in Indianapolis at the time. Richardson, who examined Washington when she went to the hospital the day after agreeing to visit Tyson, said she had abrasions consistent with sexual assault. Other beauty pageant witnesses who had also met Tyson around the time of the allegations noted his forthcoming nature regarding his intentions. One recalled how Tyson would go from girl to girl asking if they wanted to date, highlighting some intentionally steered clear of him as a result. Tyson's testimony in court appeared to back up those accounts as he admitted in court: “I explained to her that I wanted to f*** her." He maintains his innocence and belief the encounter was completely consensual in the documentary, saying: "She never said 'no'. I didn't cross a line." An account from Tyson's chauffeur at the time, Virginia Foster, also worked against his defence. Foster testified under oath that Washington looked more dishevelled and appeared to be "in a state of shock" when she returned to the limousine in the early hours of the morning. Foster also alleged Tyson had previously exposed himself to her in a hotel room and made advances on a separate occasion. Trump's relationship with Tyson appears to be alive and well today. Just this week, Tyson appeared at a Trump rally in Syracuse, New York, ahead of the US mid-term elections and called him "my president." Addressing a crowd of Republican supporters, he added: "There's no way in the world I would ever be here if it wasn't for a president like Donald Trump." news.title: Liberal senator's scathing dig at Mehreen Faruqi as Green takes extraordinary step of Albo for 'taking selfies' wth Trump because he is 'participant in genocide'
news.text:
The mere act of meeting Donald Trump is beyond the pale for Mehreen Faruqi - with the Greens senator slamming Prime Minister Anthony Albanese for taking 'selfies with one of the active participants of genocide' during his recent trip to New York. 

Faruqi made the extraordinary comments on the Senate floor on Tuesday during a fiery sitting where One Nation leader Pauline Hanson condemned both her and independent senator Lidia Thorpe as a 'disgrace'. 

Senators Faruqi and Thorpe both sought to suspend parliamentary standing orders and force debate on motions relating to Gaza, with Faruqi accusing the Albanese government of failing to act through what she described as 'three years of genocide'. 

During a lengthy diatribe, Faruqi said: 'Three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza, three years of mass murder of Palestinians, three years of killing more than 21,000 Palestinian children. 

'This government can't call these atrocities and war crimes what they really are, which is genocide.'

The Greens senator also targeted Albanese personally, claiming Labor had spent years attempting to silence critics of Israel rather than taking action. 

'I've said before that the Prime Minister has never met a billionaire he didn't love,' she said. 

She then criticised Albanese's recent interactions with US President Donald Trump, while he was in New York City for the United Nations General Assembly earlier this month. 

'Watching him take selfies with one of the active participants of this genocide,' she said.

'Our government chooses to cosy up with Trump, who is a warmonger whose barbaric ideas include threats to annihilate Iran.'

Liberal senator Andrew Bragg could be heard mocking Faruqi's criticism of Israel and support for Iran.

'Excellent government in that country,' he said, in reference to Iran's ruling Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which is listed as a terrorist organisation in Australia. 

Australian authorities have linked the IRGC to the 2024 fire bomb attacks of Sydney's Lewis's Continental Kitchen and Melbourne's Adass Israel Synagogue. 

Faruqi also described Trump as 'a sadistic con artist' and urged the government to 'name the atrocities for what they really are, a genocide'.

She called on Labor to expel Israel's ambassador, impose sanctions on Israel and end the two-way arms trade.

Shortly afterwards, Senator Thorpe mounted her own bid to suspend standing orders, using much of her speech to accuse the Albanese government of being 'actively complicit' in genocide.

'I'm proposing the suspension of standing orders today because last week marked three years of Israel's genocide against the Palestinian people,' Senator Thorpe said.

'This means three years of relentless, intentional killing, destruction and displacement. Three years of Israel using starvation as a tool for genocide.'

The independent senator claimed Australia was failing to meet its international obligations and accused the government of continuing to support Israel despite the mounting death toll.

'This country is just failing to act in the face of genocide. It is actively complicit in it,' she said.

'It continues to supply weapons parts. That's why this motion is urgent, because this government is supplying weapons to Israel to commit genocide.'

Thorpe argued there could be no more pressing issue before Parliament than the conflict in Gaza.

'There could be no more urgent reason to suspend standing orders today and every other day than to act in line with our most fundamental human rights obligation to prevent and stop genocide,' she said.

She also warned that failing to hold Israel accountable for alleged breaches of international law 'sets a dangerous precedent' and accused the government of refusing to take meaningful action.

Both senators' motions were ultimately defeated when Labor, the Coalition and One Nation voted against them.
news.summary: The mere act of meeting Donald Trump is beyond the pale for Mehreen Faruqi.
news.author: Editor,Nicholas Comino

news.title: ‘India is main focus in Asia’: Catalonia Business Minister Rodriguez eyes doubling trade in 5 years
news.text:
Over the past decade, trade between India and Spain's Catalonia region has doubled, and Business Minister Miquel Samper Rodriguez expects it to double again over the next five years and expand into sectors that will shape the future.
In an interview with Firstpost in Delhi, Rodriguez said he was in India for two main reasons. "Firstly, politically and economically, India is the main focus of our Asia strategy. Secondly, we are exploring market access and investments. India is a key market for Catalan businesses. Its economy is growing at a rate that is twice the global average, and it has already become the world's most populous country."
Last year, India became Catalonia's 15th-largest trading partner. The region imported €2.24 billion worth of goods from India, while exports stood at around €624.8 million. Rodriguez said the Catalan government is convinced that this outlook will improve once the India-EU trade agreement comes into force.
"The India-EU trade agreement allows India and Europe to be each other's stable and reliable partner. Without a doubt, there will be a before and after period in the relationship once it's in force. As European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described it, this is 'the mother of all deals'. Given the scale of both markets, the agreement is expected to eliminate or reduce barriers for more than 90 per cent of EU exports to India," said Rodriguez.
The visit to India was aimed at laying the groundwork for the future of the India-Catalonia trade relationship. Rodriguez held consultations with officials, industry bodies, and business executives during the trip. He also signed multiple agreements, including one with Nasscom in the field of emerging technologies such as semiconductors and a memorandum of understanding with the Automotive Component Manufacturers Association of India.
Catalonia Trade & Investment is expanding its presence in India and will open its second office in New Delhi this year. It already operates an office in Mumbai.
"India is clearly becoming an increasingly strategic market for the international growth of Catalan companies. It is a market we are committed to promoting and bringing closer to our business community. To support this ambition, we are also strengthening our presence on the ground through the opening of a new Catalonia Trade and Investment office in New Delhi," said Rodriguez.
Just like with EU, India-Catalonia ties seek a win-win arrangement
In recent years, as the world has grappled with supply-chain disruptions and the weaponisation of trade, India and Europe have moved closer together. That trend has been accelerated by US President Donald Trump's tariffs and political pressures that both sides have faced.
Observers have highlighted that India and Europe are naturally compatible because their economies are largely complementary rather than directly competitive. Europe generally sells what India wants but does not produce and while India largely exports what Europe needs but does not manufacture itself. The same dynamic applies to India and Catalonia. Catalonia's principal exports to India include chemical products, metals, and machinery, while its principal imports include chemicals, fuels, and clothing.
While this complementary relationship has helped double trade over the past decade, the future is expected to be even more synergistic.
"The India-EU trade agreement will also improve market access for services, including financial and maritime services, and includes a framework for joint innovation in technologies, startup partnerships, and collaborative projects in hydrogen, artificial intelligence, and high-performance computing. These are all strategic sectors and technologies of major importance for Catalonia," said Rodriguez.
During the visit, Rodriguez noted southern India's strong focus on technology and said Catalonia is "going to establish cooperation links, through the two offices, with all the regions where we can contribute our knowledge and combine it with what exists in India".
But Catalonia is not seeking only trade and investment. Rodriguez said the region also welcomes Indian talent.
"Catalonia is already home to Indian companies operating in sectors such as pharmaceuticals, machinery, capital goods, chemicals, food and beverage, and information and communication technologies. These sectors are among the pillars of our economy, and we warmly welcome the highly skilled talent that supports these investments and growth projects. We are confident that their expertise, innovation, and international outlook will continue to contribute to the competitiveness and growth of the Catalan economy," said Rodriguez.
In both Catalonia and India, the wheels are turning. As officials prepare to open the second trade and investment office in New Delhi, Rodriguez expects to return to India and take forward the discussions initiated during this visit with various stakeholders.
"The relationship between Catalonia and India already has a strong foundation, but we believe there is significant potential for further growth. India is a major global economic powerhouse and a market of particular interest to Catalonia due to its expertise in areas such as ICT, industry, and research services, among many others. We also share a strong entrepreneurial culture with vibrant startup ecosystems that are driving innovation and creating high-impact projects with the potential to transform entire industries. We have no doubt that Indian talent and entrepreneurship can make a valuable contribution to Catalonia's business ecosystem," said Rodriguez.
news.author: Madhur Sharma

news.title: Trump Gets Brutally Fact-Checked For Claiming Denzel Washington Called Him A ‘Great Friend’
news.text:
Trump shared a social media post from the X account “Red Eagle Updates” that alleged that the Oscar winner had nothing but praise for the president, and even considered him a “great friend.” 

“BOOM: Denzel Washington: ‘I’ve worked with a lot of people in my life, and I’ve never met anyone braver, smarter, or who cares more about America than Donald Trump. He’s a great friend and an even better president. I’m proud to be a steadfast supporter and I’ll never apologize for it,’” the original post read. 

The post then asked social media users if they agreed with Washington’s so-called words. 

The fact-checking website Snopes revealed that Trump’s repost is 100% false, noting that it had “found no reporting that Washington spoke favorably of Trump” on major news outlets like ABC News, CBS News, CNN, Fox News or others.

The website added, “If any actor of Washington’s prominence who had never publicly expressed such support in the past were to say the words attributed to them in the meme, national and international outlets covering entertainment and politics would have widely reported it.” 

HuffPost has reached out to the White House and reps for Washington for comment. 

The rumor-debunking site said that the same phony quote from Washington had also been previously attributed to actor Matthew McConaughey and Rolling Stones’ lead singer, Mick Jagger, in memes across social media. 

Snopes also fact-checked erroneous reporting from 2018 that claimed that Washington said that electing Trump saved the U.S. from becoming an “Orwellian police state.”

Washington has generally abstained from aligning with political parties, and has criticized both the left and the right. 

Speaking with the UK’s The Times in November 2024, Washington urged the public to realize they’re “being manipulated by both sides.”

news.title: After surging troops to the border, US Army showcases a quieter Rio Grande
news.text:
Published: 00:26 EDT, 13 October 2026 | Updated: 00:26 EDT, 13 October 2026

ROMA, Texas (AP) – Standing on a high bank of the Rio Grande, Army Lt. Col. Ray Richards points to a stretch of river that was, until recently, one of the busiest spots for illegal border crossings from Mexico.

But on a recent afternoon, the area is quiet. American soldiers gather at a border monitoring post in Roma, Texas, where an infantry vehicle with camouflage netting sits between houses. A Blackhawk helicopter drops soldiers onto an island in the river, while U.S. Border Patrol agents breeze by on fan-propelled boats.

“At any given time, there would be multiple rafts full of people trying to get to this side,” Richards said of the area before U.S. forces made it a priority last year.

The Army has been inviting reporters to the Rio Grande Valley as it deploys hundreds more soldiers to the region this month by shifting some of the thousands of troops already serving along the 2,000-mile border. U.S. officials said the troop surge follows signs of elevated activity from drug cartels and has been accompanied by increased cooperation from the Mexican military. The U.S. Coast Guard said it recently encountered gunfire from the Mexican side of the river, prompting the Americans to fire back.

In this small patch at the southern edge of the United States, a slow saga is playing out – a curious mix of policing, policy and politics.

While Republicans face increasing headwinds because of President Donald Trump´s unpopularity, persistently high prices and the fallout from the war in Iran, border security has remained a relative bright spot in Trump’s polling numbers, with about half of Americans saying they approve of his performance there.

Troops disembark from a U.S. Army helicopter on an island along the Rio Grande in Roma, Texas, Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Eric Gay)

But some experts have questioned the need for such a large military presence. They suggest it’s less about effective strategy and more about political theater.

Illegal crossings have plummeted due in large part to asylum restrictions that began before Trump returned to the White House. Meanwhile, a large percentage of the fentanyl, cocaine and heroin seized along the border was being smuggled in cars and trucks passing through checkpoints, not the areas in between.

David Shirk, a University of San Diego political science professor, said the Trump administration wants to remind voters it’s been very aggressive on border security.

“I don’t dispute there´s some benefit to having personnel in areas at risk for people smuggling and drug trafficking,” Shirk said. “But the vast majority of that is now happening at ports of entry.”

Dessa Bergen-Cico, a professor of public health at Syracuse University who studies drug trafficking, said street prices for cocaine and fentanyl are still low, suggesting the drug flow remains unimpeded.

But Army Maj. Gen. Curtis Taylor, who commands the military’s southern border task force, said the work has been vital and effective, particularly for targeting human trafficking.

The moral argument for the Army’s mission is “dismantling this marketplace of human trafficking that is bringing people into the border,” Taylor said. “An added benefit of that is there´s an awful lot of drugs moving with that human trafficking.”

Roma, a city of about 10,000 people, lacks a border wall in some places because homes sit close to the steep slopes along the Rio Grande. Directly across the water is Miguel Alemán, a town in the Mexican state of Tamaulipas that´s been plagued by decades of cartel violence. From Roma, it’s a football field’s distance across the river at best and much less in some places.

In 2021, Roma became a center of illegal crossings when thousands of families and unaccompanied children arrived each day to seek asylum. Border crossings fell sharply after President Joe Biden introduced severe asylum restrictions in 2024 and dipped after Trump suspended asylum at the border.

After Trump returned to the White House in January 2025, the Army and Coast Guard expanded operations to back up the Border Patrol, which remains the lead agency for border security. The Army now commands some 8,000 U.S. troops along the entire border, while the U.S. Coast Guard and Texas law enforcement have brought in more personnel.

Army officials said people still try to cross into Roma despite multiple obstacles. A barrier of strung-together buoys, each the size of a hay bale, stretched along the river. Concertina wire lined the U.S. river bank, while a surveillance blimp hung in the sky. A river island was recently cleared of trees that hid people trying to cross.

Army Sgt. Nathaniel Decker said he recently saw people on three rafts set out from the Mexican side at dusk. He reported to Border Patrol that one group had cleared the buoys. They were eventually caught by a house in Roma.

The U.S. has stopped many of the drones used by the cartels to surveil the border and ferry drugs, by electronically jamming or capturing them or shooting them down with a laser.

The U.S. has gotten better at tracking them and coordinating with Mexican officials to locate the drones’ operators. But some still get across.

“We have reduced a lot of the flights,” said Richards, the Army lieutenant colonel, who has deployed with the Massachusetts Army National Guard. “But in the middle of the night, those drones can fly into the U.S. airspace, and that´s a true threat to any soldier on the ground.”

Under pressure from Trump, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has cracked down more heavily on crime than her predecessors. Mexico this month sent 500 National Guard and military officers to Tamaulipas as part of a coordinated effort with the U.S. to prevent drug and human trafficking.

Mexico’s deployment “is based on intelligence gathered regarding the movements of criminal groups,” a federal official in Mexico told The Associated Press, speaking on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to comment on the matter.

As part of the operation, the Mexican Army is using two UH-60 helicopters, drones and anti-drone equipment.

The U.S. Coast Guard has also boosted patrols on the Rio Grande, bringing in more than 300 personnel in October of last year. While stopping a boat on the river last month, the Coast Guard encountered gunfire from the Mexican side of the water near Garceno, Texas, the service said in a statement. The Americans returned fire. None were hurt.

U.S. Coast Guard Cmdr. Jeff Miller wouldn’t give additional details about the exchange of gunfire, except to say the personnel are “working in a very challenging environment” and are authorized to use force to protect themselves.

On a recent patrol, the scene along the river was quiet. A Coast Guard boat armed with machine guns motored along the greenish water. Two men fished from a small boat. A privately funded border wall, made from galvanized steel, lined the American side. In Mexico, there was a park with soccer goal posts, homes and a woman waving.

A Coast Guardsman driving the boat, who declined to give his name, said he’s seen kids on the Mexican side get excited as if a fire truck were passing. Others have offered the Americans cold beer. Some have reacted with offensive gestures.

Joel Garcia, Border Patrol’s acting deputy chief patrol agent for the Rio Grande Valley, said the agency has proof that U.S. operations have been effective based on the amount of drug seizures, the number of people apprehended and decreasing traffic within certain areas.

“Border security, when done right, if we have truly secured the line, should be boring,” he added. “It should look as if no one is crossing and nothing is happening.”

Associated Press writers Fabiola Sánchez and Megan Janetsky in Mexico City contributed to this report.

news.title: Jimmy Kimmel Hits Back After Trump Calls Him a ‘Loser’ for Rally Size Crack: ‘Let’s Do It Again’
news.text:
Jimmy Kimmel mocked Donald Trump after the president blasted him as a “loser” for making a dig about his rally size.

During Monday’s monologue on “Jimmy Kimmel Live!,” the comedian addressed Trump’s remarks at a Saturday rally in Clarksville, Tenn., where the president called the late night host a “loser” and “crooked.”

“This loser, Jimmy Kimmel. What a loser,” the president said in a clip aired on “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” “I had just left Texas or somewhere. The place is packed. And maybe it was Ohio, place is packed. He said, ‘Donald Trump had a sparsely attended [rally].’ I said, ‘Sparsely attended?!’ They had to walk thousands of people – they couldn’t get into the [event]. These guys are crooked people. They’re losers.”

In response to the call out, Kimmel quipped, “Do I really sound like that? Be honest.”

“Of all the things I said about him last week. Of all the many moronic and criminal words and deeds I detailed, that’s what bothers him?! Me pointing out the fact that his rallies have empty seats??” Kimmel said. “Well, in that case, let’s do it again. There were many empty seats at the rally. So many empty seats.”

The “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” editors then cut to images of empty seats at Trump’s rally.

“There were even empty seats at the rally where he complained about me saying he had empty seats at the rally,” Kimmel said. “He keeps claiming the reason there are empty seats in the back and the top is because the people love him so much they make their way down to the front. Isn’t it interesting that that never happens at a Lakers game? People just moving up to the front. But it does at an event controlled by the United States Secret Service.”

Kimmel then claimed that the president’s rallies were “not at full capacity,” much like “Trump’s cognitive function.”

Watch Kimmel’s full monologue below. A representative for the White House did not immediately respond to TheWrap’s request for comment.

Kimmel is not the only figured to face Trump’s wrath over rally coverage. Last week, Trump called for media outlets to be arrested over rally coverage, blasting it as a “disservice.”

“The Ohio Arena was already full to the brim — and yet these people were still trying to get in,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “The New York Times said, ‘There were empty seats’ when, in fact, there were none, and thousands of people had to be turned away. The New York Times, and many other Artificial Media Outlets, should be arrested for their dishonesty and disservice to our Country. When Bernie Sanders has 500 to 1,000 people, they make it sound like it’s the biggest event that ever took place. When PRESIDENT DONALD J. TRUMP has 50,000 people, they make it sound like nobody showed up!”

news.title: Russia Launches Missile and Drone Attacks Across Ukraine – Two Killed in Kyiv Despite Trump’s Ceasefire Claim
news.text:
Russian forces launched waves of missile and drone attacks across Ukraine from Monday, Oct. 12, into early Tuesday, Oct. 13, killing two women in Kyiv, leaving 11 people affected in Kharkiv and damaging residential buildings near Lviv and in other regions.

n Kyiv, Russia fired six ballistic missiles late Monday, striking transport and warehouse facilities hours after a drone hit a residential complex, killing two women and wounding nine people.

In Kharkiv, Russian missiles devastated residential neighborhoods, destroying an entire entrance section of a four-story apartment building. Three people were rescued from the rubble.

Ukraine’s Air Force said the ballistic missiles targeted several districts at around 10:10 p.m. local time.

Ukrainian radar detected the incoming missiles, but the military said it had received no advance information about launches from Russian territory.

The Air Force said it was investigating the circumstances, while the missile types had not yet been established.

The attacks continued late into the night, with renewed warnings of incoming Russian drones.

Two women killed in Kyiv as missiles strike infrastructure

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko confirmed missile impacts in two districts on the capital’s left bank.

In the Dniprovskyi district, a missile struck a transport infrastructure facility, while another hit a four-story warehouse in the Desnianskyi district.

Emergency services were dispatched to both locations, Klitschko reported on Telegram.

Earlier Monday, a Russian drone struck the courtyard of a residential complex in Kyiv’s Darnytskyi district, causing fires inside the building and igniting parked vehicles.

Ukraine’s National Police confirmed that two women, aged 39 and 59, were killed and nine people wounded, including a minor.

Investigators, explosives specialists and emergency crews worked at the scene, documenting damage and collecting evidence, according to the official police statement.

Earlier in the day, Russian drone strikes and falling debris damaged homes and other civilian buildings across several Kyiv districts.

Police reported damage in six districts, including three private homes in Darnytskyi and two preschools in Solomianskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts.

Children and staff at both educational institutions had taken shelter, preventing casualties there.

At 11:17 p.m., authorities warned of another drone threat, urging Kyiv residents to remain in shelters.

Kharkiv missile barrage leaves 11 casualties, three rescued

Russian missile strikes on Kharkiv late Monday left 11 people injured or otherwise affected, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service (DSNS).

The attacks struck the Kholodnohirskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts, destroying an entire entrance section of a four-story residential building.

Three people were rescued from the rubble, while a rescue worker was injured during emergency operations and hospitalized.

Kharkiv Regional Military Administration head Oleh Syniehubov said Russian forces had used approximately 10 Banderol-type missiles, according to preliminary information.

Among the wounded was a 19-year-old man admitted to intensive care with severe burns. Another seriously injured man required surgery.

At least 10 private homes were damaged in Kholodnohirskyi district.

In Shevchenkivskyi district, another strike hit a five-story apartment building, setting fire to ground-floor bank premises and several vehicles.

Emergency teams continued clearing debris and searching for possible survivors.

Russian drone sets two homes ablaze near Lviv

The attacks reached western Ukraine early Tuesday, when a downed Russian drone fell onto a residential building in the village of Murovane, near Lviv.

According to Lviv Regional Military Administration head Maksym Kozytskyi, the incident occurred during an air raid alert.

Two houses caught fire, and three vehicles were damaged.

No casualties had been reported at the time of the initial update, while emergency services worked at the site.

The strike brought the overnight destruction to western Ukraine, far from the front lines, as Russian drones continued threatening residential communities across the country.

Kharkiv missile barrage leaves 11 casualties, three rescued

In northeastern Ukraine, Russian missile strikes on Kharkiv late Monday left 11 people injured or otherwise affected, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service (DSNS).

The attack struck the Kholodnohirskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts, destroying an entire entrance section of a four-story residential building.

Rescuers pulled three people to safety, while another rescue worker was injured during emergency operations and hospitalized.

Kharkiv Regional Military Administration head Oleh Syniehubov said Russia had used approximately 10 Banderol-type missiles, according to preliminary information.

Among the wounded was a 19-year-old man admitted to intensive care with severe burns. Another seriously injured man required surgery.

At least 10 private homes were damaged in Kholodnohirskyi district.

In Shevchenkivskyi district, a separate strike hit a five-story apartment building, triggering fires in a ground-floor bank premises and nearby vehicles.

Emergency crews continued clearing debris and searching for possible survivors, according to the latest DSNS report.

Russian attacks damage homes and dormitories in Rivne region

Russian forces also attacked Rivne and surrounding areas on Monday evening, damaging residential buildings and civilian facilities.

Regional Military Administration head Oleksandr Koval said a nonresidential building was damaged in Rivne, with no casualties initially reported.

In Sarny district, several strikes hit a nonoperational industrial facility. Residential buildings and dormitories were also damaged.

Koval urged residents near the impact sites to move at least 100 meters away while authorities assessed the damage.

The latest strikes followed an attack on Rivne region on Sunday, Oct. 11, which wounded three people. 

Russian drones kill woman in Lozova, strike logistics hub in Mykolaiv

Elsewhere in Kharkiv region, Russian drones struck the city of Lozova on Monday, killing a 71-year-old woman and leaving seven people suffering from acute stress, including a nine-year-old girl.

Two fires broke out in residential areas after the strikes, according to emergency officials.

Prosecutors said preliminary evidence indicated that Russia had used two Geran-3 drones.

In southern Ukraine, a Russian Shahed-type drone struck a cargo terminal in Mykolaiv, damaging a logistics facility and sparking a fire.

Emergency crews extinguished a blaze covering approximately 500 square meters. No casualties were reported, according to regional authorities.

In Sloviansk, Donetsk region, Russian forces carried out another strike while emergency crews were extinguishing a fire caused by an earlier attack.

A woman was injured and 44 residential buildings were damaged, according to the State Emergency Service.

Zelensky urges US pressure as Russian strikes continue despite ceasefire announcement

The nationwide attacks followed US President Donald Trump’s announcement on Sunday, Oct. 11, that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to an energy ceasefire – a claim neither government had publicly confirmed.

During his evening address Monday, President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned Russia’s continuing strikes and urged Washington to act decisively.

“It is Russia that continues these brutal strikes. It is Russia that is prolonging the war. Even now, in response to the American proposal, it is sending Shahed drones,” Zelensky said.

“We hope the United States will recognize these signals from Russia and act decisively. Strength is needed to force Russia to end this war,” he added.

Zelensky said Ukraine was prepared to suspend long-range attacks on Russian oil refineries and export facilities if Moscow stopped targeting Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

But Russia’s continued strikes raised questions about whether the Kremlin intended to observe any reciprocal ceasefire.

The attacks also came amid controversy over Washington’s decision to temporarily ease restrictions on Russian diesel exports, despite Ukraine’s calls for stronger economic pressure on Moscow.
news.summary: Russian missile and drone attacks swept across Ukraine from Monday, Oct. 12, into early Tuesday, Oct. 13, killing two women and wounding nine people in Kyiv. Russia launched approximately six ballistic missiles at the capital, hitting transport and warehouse facilities. Near Lviv, a downed drone set two houses ablaze, while a massive missile attack on Kharkiv left 11 people affected and three rescued from rubble. Rivne also reported damage from Russian strikes.
news.author: Kyiv Post

news.title: Nato warns Russia of tough response to any attack
news.text:
BRUSSELS: Nato’s top commander warned Russia on Monday that his forces would destroy “anything and everything” involved in any attack if Moscow was “foolish enough” to launch an assault on alliance territory.

Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich stressed Nato was a defensive alliance. But he outlined a three-pronged approach of blocking, blunting and breaking enemy forces to make any attack “utterly futile”.

His remarks come amid heightened tensions between Europe and Russia and lingering concerns among European allies over US President Donald Trump’s commitment to Nato’s mutual defence pact.

In recent days, Trump has announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin allowing Russia to supply diesel to global markets and renewed his criticism of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

European govts seek Nato assurance over Moscow’s ‘clandestine operations of arson, drone incursions and cyber disruptions’

European governments accuse Moscow of stepping up a campaign of sabotage, drone incursions and cyberattacks against them, while Russia warned last month it could use nuclear weapons if Nato attempted to cut off its Kaliningrad exclave. Grynkewich did not mention Russia by name but much of his message was clearly directed at Moscow. Nato’s 2022 Strategic Concept describes Russia as the alliance’s most significant security threat.

“If someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight,” he said. “We will, in short, ensure any attack, against any ally, proves utterly futile.” Grynkewich said Nato’s response would not be limited to forces involved in an initial attack. “Should the adversary choose to press the attack or commit his reserves, we will break the warfighting system engaged against us,” he said.

“This includes not just the attacking force itself, but anything and everything that supports, sustains, and controls that force.” Putin said this month Russia had no plans to attack any European country and wanted to coexist peacefully. Such declarations have not reassured European leaders, given Russia made similar statements before the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Russia has also repeatedly denied involvement in sabotage and other hybrid operations.

Allies reassured

Grynkewich said he had decided to talk publicly about Nato’s plans because recent acts of sabotage and arson had made people around the alliance nervous. “What I want to do is assure the one billion citizens of our alliance that we’ve got this. We know what we need to do. We know how we would do it,” he said.

He said he also wanted to send a message to anyone considering harming Nato members. Grynkewich sought to downplay concerns about Washington’s commitment to the alliance, recalling that Trump spoke of “love” at a Nato summit in Ankara in July. “I was in the room and I felt the love,” he said.

news.title: MAGA News Channel Cuts Away as Interview Goes Off the Rails
news.text:
A right-wing channel abruptly cut away from an interview with a Donald Trump rallygoer after the segment quickly derailed.

During coverage of Trump’s rally in Youngstown, Ohio on Monday, Real America’s Voice cut to Bobby McNeily, a reporter for the Pro-Trump network. McNeily, who was inside the arena, introduced an interview with a man he spoke with earlier while he was waiting in line. The man was identified as Brian. 

McNeily opened by riffing on Brian’s Forrest Gump T-shirt, quoting the movie’s “I just felt like running” line and adding, “I love that movie.” Then the bit fell apart. 

Looking baffled, McNeily told viewers he was “hearing from friends” that the man beside him was “not a fan of President Trump.” 

“It’s very interesting,” McNeily said, “because I’ve never really spoken to anyone that I can recall, interviewing them, not a fan of President Trump, but standing in line to see him. Brian then revealed that it was his first Trump rally.

“What are you hoping to hear tonight?” McNeily asked. 

“What I hope to hear is not what I plan to hear… what I plan to hear is a bunch of rhetoric, a bunch of lies, a bunch of the same old script, that sort of stuff,” Brian said. 

“I’m here to get a firsthand perspective of the kind of lies and garbage and stuff that he’s going to probably be peddling for the next two years, as if the first two haven’t been bad enough.”

“Do you consider yourself a registered Democrat, or how would you vote before?” McNeily asked. 

“I was independent, because I consider myself moderate,” he said. 

“I was independent until JD Vance entered our ballot, and then I actually registered for a Republican. My strategy being, if I can keep him off the general election ballot by voting against him in a primary, then I get two chances to eliminate all these MAGA idiots. That’s my approach.” 

McNeily then followed up with a question about whether Vance’s selection had encouraged him.

“Oh, I can’t stand him,” Brian said. “I mean, it’s basically anybody that endorses or is endorsed by Donald is not a fan of mine.”

Moments later, the interview cut away from Brian mid-sentence. The network then cut back to a studio panel, including McNeily, who were asked for a “quick reaction.”

Host Grant Stinchfield marveled at how politely he thought Brian had been treated. 

“The left would not be as nice to us if we were at a, God forbid, Kamala Harris rally,” he said. “But he’s Trump-deranged, isn’t he?”

“Absolutely, Grant,” McNeily replied. Still, he said he was “holding out hope” for Brian. “I’m an optimistic guy.”

McNeily guessed that Brian had “listened to crazy far left outlets instead of actually really seeking the truth in all of this.”

The rally came three weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections. 

Trump was in Youngstown to campaign for Sen. Jon Husted, 59. The Republican was appointed to Vance’s old seat in 2025, after Vance became vice president. Husted is trailing former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown as the GOP fights to hold onto a state Trump won by double digits in 2024, according to the Hill. 

Trump’s swing through Ohio comes as his approval ratings hit historic lows. A Pew Research Center poll released last week found that only three in ten Americans now approve of the way Donald Trump is handling his job as president.

The Daily Beast has reached out to the White House and Real America’s Voice for comment.
news.summary:
RAVA right-wing channel abruptly cut away from an interview with a Donald Trump rallygoer after the segment quickly derailed.

During coverage of Trump’s rally in Youngstown, Ohio on Monday, Real America’s Voice cut to Bobby McNeily, a reporter for the Pro-Trump network. McNeily, who was inside the arena, introduced an interview with a man he spoke with earlier while he was waiting in line. The man was identified as Brian. 

McNeily opened by riffing on Brian’s Forrest Gump T-shirt, quoting the movie’s “I just felt like running” line and adding, “I love that movie.” Then the bit fell apart. 

Read more at The Daily Beast.

news.title: Crude oil futures fall after nearly $2 gain in previous session
news.text:
Crude oil futures traded lower on Tuesday morning after rising nearly $2 a barrel in the previous trading session, as markets assessed the impact of Russian diesel exports amid rising tensions in West Asia.

At 9.30 am on Tuesday, December Brent oil futures were at $105.42, down by 1.15 per cent, and November crude oil futures on WTI (West Texas Intermediate) were at $92.63, down by 1.18 per cent. October crude oil futures were trading at ₹8850 on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) during the initial hour of trading on Tuesday against the previous close of ₹8980, down by 1.45 per cent, and November futures were trading at ₹8800, against the previous close of ₹8935, down by 1.51 per cent.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on Monday that Russia will be able to return diesel exports to levels above those US President Donald Trump has outlined under a deal with Russia.

Speaking to Rossiya-24 state TV channel, Novak said: “We will see how the situation develops further, but Russia has the capacity to increase diesel fuel exports. By the end of the year, exports could reach 3-3.5 million tonnes ⁠per month, returning to the levels seen before the crisis,” he said.

In their Commodities Feed for Tuesday, Warren Patterson, Head of Commodities Strategy of ING Think, and Ewa Manthey, Commodities Strategist, said the weakness in the oil market following Trump’s announcement of an ‘energy ceasefire’ between Russia and the Ukraine was short-lived. That goes, too, for the US-Russia diesel export deal.

“ICE Brent settled 1.8 per cent higher, just shy of $107 a barrel on Monday — the highest close since mid-September. Clearly, the market is more concerned over recent developments in West Asia, with Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and the lingering risks to oil flows from the Persian Gulf. In addition, there’s considerable scepticism over the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire, particularly with reports that Russia has hit Ukrainian energy targets since Trump announced it. While diesel initially saw some weakness following the US-Russia deal, strength has returned. The volumes suggested are doing little to offset the tightness in the global middle distillate market,” they said.

The Persian Gulf could see further bypass volumes in a relatively short time period. The Saudi Energy Minister said that the country is looking to expand its pipeline export capacity to 10 million barrels a day, up from a current 7 million barrels a day. About 1.2 million barrels a day of this expansion could come from converting a gas pipeline to crude and could be available to transport oil within 7-8 weeks. Expansion beyond this would take more time, possibly as much as three years. Shipping larger volumes from the Red Sea would also require further investment in loading capacity at ports, they said.

Meanwhile, hurricane activity in the Gulf of Mexico continues to disrupt offshore operations for US producers; they have shut in almost 605,000 barrels a day of oil production, which is equivalent to nearly 30 per cent of total US production in the Gulf of Mexico, according to the Marine Minerals Administration. However, output has been recovering in recent days, with as much as 1.5 million barrels a day shut-in on Friday, they said.
